items.title: Ben Kelly Interview, 1960-08-11
items.q: Interviewer mentions 'Norwood' as a clarinet player who didn't stay with the band; Interviewee confirms the name but does not describe a personal interaction or professional relationship with Norwood.

ctx.x: Jim Robinson. He played with him in the band. He had this boy, Chita Howell. He come up, Chris taught him he used to be a drummer. My brother broke him off the drum. Put him on a trumpet and made him famous during this time. Who was the clarinet player with the band? Do you remember who played clarinet? Well, they had one fellow that had to try to play clarinet, but he never did make

famous so he just put it down. Do you remember his name? Yeah. Called him Norwood. What was the name again? No, Norwood. Norwood. Yeah. Oh, no. Norwood. But he put it down. He didn't stay with it? No. Do you remember who he had then later?

Didn't use no. Didn't use clarinet or something? No. All he used was trumpet, big instruments, baritone, solo alto, voice alto, drum. This is the brass band you're talking about? Yeah, the brass band. Now in the string band which they had, they used clarinet. But that's uh, he's dead and gone. That's uh, Jim Riddler, uncle. Sam Robinson. Oh, Sam Robinson. Yeah. That was the clarinet player. Was that a brother of Jim Robinson's, the trombonist, his brother? Yeah. His brother. Yeah. He told us a little bit about…
